items.name: Location
items.summary: Represents a location, determined by a line and a column number, in the original SQL query.

items.name: Span
items.summary: Represents an interval of characters in the original SQL query.

methods.name: new
methods.signature: fn new(start: Location, end: Location) -> Self
methods.summary: Creates a new [`Span`] from a start and an end [`Location`].

methods.name: try_from_sqlparser_span
methods.summary: Convert a [`Span`](sqlparser::tokenizer::Span) from the parser, into a DataFusion [`Span`]. If the input span is empty (line 0 column 0, to line 0 column 0), then [`None`] is returned.

methods.name: union
methods.summary: Returns the smallest Span that contains both `self` and `other`

methods.name: union_iter
methods.signature: fn union_iter<I: IntoIterator<Item = Span>>(iter: I) -> Option<Span>
methods.summary: Return the [Span::union] of all spans in the iterator.

items.name: Spans
items.summary: A collection of [`Span`], meant to be used as a field of entities whose location in the original SQL query is desired to be tracked. Sometimes an entity can have multiple spans. e.g. if you want to track the position of the column a that c…

methods.name: first
methods.summary: Returns the first [`Span`], if any. This is useful when you know that there's gonna be only one [`Span`] at most.

methods.name: new
methods.summary: Creates a new empty [`Spans`] with no [`Span`].
